thread:
Priya: Hey team -- starting an international adoption process and looking into Redwood's leave + legal stipend. Timeline is uncertain (could be 8-12 weeks notice), but I want to prepare paperwork and coverage. What forms do I need, and is the legal/adoption stipend handled automatically or do I submit receipts? Also what do we do about benefits enrollment if the adoption finalizes after leave?

Dina: Congrats Priya! :tada: Short answers: 1) Submit LOA (Leave of Absence) when you know tentative travel/start dates. 2) Adoption/legal stipend is reimbursable -- keep receipts and submit the Adoption Reimbursement form after expenses. 3) Benefits changes (adding dependent) use the Benefits Enrollment Change form within 30 days of finalization. I'll DM links.

people-ops-bot: Automated: LOA form: /forms/leave | Adoption Reimbursement: /forms/adoption-reimbursement | Benefits change: /forms/benefits-change. Payroll cutoff note: reimbursements processed on next payroll cycle after docs submitted.

Mark: From an engineering coverage perspective: please create a 1-page handoff + list of active execs we talk to for the external vendor. I'll assign Luis as scheduled backup for the period you expect to travel. If timeline shifts, flag asap.

Priya: Thanks Mark. Timeline could be a 10-day travel window followed by paperwork wait. Is the stipend capped? Also are travel costs reimbursed or just legal fees?

Dina: Adoption stipend: up to $8,000 per Redwood policy for domestic/international (checks policy link). Reimbursable items include legal fees, adoption agency fees, travel reasonably necessary for the adoption (airfare, lodging). Please retain itemized receipts and a short expense summary. If you prefer advance payment, we can discuss a lump-sum advance — request via People Ops and include estimated costs; approval is discretionary and may require manager signoff.

Luis: I can take over the oncall rotation weeks while you're traveling. Priya if you can paste your oncall runbook + who to page (pagerduty group) I'll sync with Mark and test handoff 48h before travel.

Priya: Will do. And regarding state/provincial leave laws: does Redwood combine company parental leave with local statutory pay? I may have to claim from another country's system.

Dina: Good question. We coordinate statutory leave from the local jurisdiction with company top-up. For international cases we work case-by-case: submit the LOA + any local claim docs to People Ops. We'll calculate top-up relative to the statutory benefit you're eligible for. Please include the country and expected dates on the LOA so we can confirm payroll/tax implications.

Priya: Got it. One more: if final paperwork completes after the 12 weeks, can I extend unpaid leave?

Dina: You can request an extension (unpaid/paid PTO run concurrently) — that request is processed as an LOA extension and needs manager approval. Provide anticipated end date and coverage plan.

Mark: For hiring ops: if this ends up >12 weeks we should discuss a temporary contract support for 1-2 sprints. I'll open a hiring ops thread and loop @talent-acquisition.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: submit LOA at least 30 days prior if possible. If travel is urgent submit LOA as soon as travel is confirmed to ensure payroll/top-up alignment.

Priya: Thanks everyone. I'll submit the LOA today with the expected travel window, upload the runbook, and collect receipts as things happen. Appreciate the help! :heart:
